races.title: State Senate, District 19
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Venus de la Cruz
cands.bio: Republican candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 19 in 2026. Owner and manager of Venus Vogue, Inc. and E&V Investments, and former owner and publisher of a bi-weekly magazine. Co-founder of a nonprofit serving military members and their families. She has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: The Civic Table (Sway voting group by Carrie Jackson) listed as an endorsement or voter guide recommendation on Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where she was born or raised, or when she moved to North Carolina. Ballotpedia names only Reid Ross High School, and the page doesn't say where that school is. We found no record of public office, so there are no deeds to report. We also found no statements from her on data centers, development, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, abortion, or red-flag laws. Her only on-the-record positions come from a single Ballotpedia survey. We found no news coverage of her, and no controversies or foreign ties.

score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Owner and manager of Venus Vogue, Inc. and E&V Investments, and former owner and publisher of a bi-weekly magazine. She has no record of elected office.
qual.why: Business ownership and management fall in the middle band. Her volunteer, church and nonprofit co-founder roles are not counted, and no legislative, policy or budget career is shown.
qual.label: Business ownership and management fall in the middle band. Her volunteer, church and nonprofit co-founder roles are not counted, and no legislative, policy or budget career is shown.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: She says she supports parents' right to choose their child's education, including opportunity scholarships, and wants strong teachers and high academic standards. This is from her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.

back-police-order.evidence: She says she will support law enforcement and advocate for resources for Cumberland County, including addressing recruitment and retention in the Sheriff's Office and detention center. She also says she will examine more state support for firefighters, EMS and other first responders.

second-amendment.evidence: She lists Second Amendment rights among her principles in her Ballotpedia survey answers.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised

cands.name: Val Applewhite
cands.bio: Democratic state senator for North Carolina Senate District 19 (Fayetteville) since January 2023. Real estate broker and retired U.S. Air Force veteran. Fayetteville city councilwoman 2007–2011. Holds a business administration bachelor's degree and an M.S. in political science.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by then-Gov. Roy Cooper in her 2022 Democratic primary against incumbent Sen. Kirk deViere.
Recommended in the 2026 'Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress' voter guide (a Sway voting group by Vote for Peace), among other Sway voter groups listed by Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Applewhite was born or raised, or when she moved to North Carolina. We found no documented stance from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration enforcement or H-1B, policing and public order, gun laws, or a campaign pledge on donor money. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys. Her campaign site covers broad themes (earn, own, build, thrive) without policy specifics. The abortion and school voucher positions come only from a Wikipedia summary, not from a primary record or her own statements.
